title: Other Chicago music around the Garrick Lounge
summary: Eddie South, Billy Taylor and Pete Brown nearby, and the Garrick's layout; Stuff Smith not getting his due.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When you were working at the Garrick and at the Two Deuces, who else was working around Chicago? What other music was being --
Well, right around the corner, let's see, Eddie South, Billy Taylor, and I can't remember who was on bass. It was really swinging in those days, you know?
Billy Taylor the bass player or Billy Taylor the piano player?

No, no, the piano player. Uh-huh. Let's see. I think I mentioned Pete Brown working in the Garrick Lounge upstairs. It was something. The Garrick was laid out something like the -- what's that club on Seventh Avenue in New York, across the street from the Copper Rail?
The Metropole, yeah. Day and night.

Yeah. This was upstairs and downstairs. And -- I can't remember, but I remember times when the Budapest Quartet used to come there to hear Stuff. Because he had something going. He was a tough man on his instrument, you know?
